  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Prompts user for a move via console and validates input against available moves.
   * Algorithm: 
   *   Loop:
   *     1. Print prompt and read string input "source->destination".
   *     2. Parse source and destination coordinates:
   *        - Column letter (e.g., 'a' -> 0, 'b' -> 1).
   *        - Row number (e.g., '1' -> 0, '2' -> 1).
   *     3. Construct a Move object from parsed Places.
   *     4. Iterate through availableMoves to check if the constructed move exists.
   *     5. If found, return the Move object; else print error message and continue loop.
   * Related Features: None
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place
   * Input: game (Game), availableMoves (List<Move>)
   * Output: The valid Move object selected by the player.
   * Pre-condition: availableMoves is not null and the game is in a state where a move can be made.
   * Post-condition: The returned Move is contained within the provided availableMoves list.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model availableMovesMany="true"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public Move nextMove(final Game game, final EList<Move> availableMoves)
  {
    Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
    while (true) {
      System.out.print("Enter move (e.g., a1->b2): ");
      String input = scanner.nextLine();
      
      try {
        String[] parts = input.split("->");
        if (parts.length != 2) throw new Exception("Invalid format");
        
        Place source = parsePlace(parts[0]);
        Place destination = parsePlace(parts[1]);
        
        for (Move move : availableMoves) {
          if (move.getSource().getX() == source.getX() && move.getSource().getY() == source.getY() &&
              move.getDestination().getX() == destination.getX() && move.getDestination().getY() == destination.getY()) {
            return move;
          }
        }
        System.out.println("Move not allowed. Try again.");
      } catch (Exception e) {
        System.out.println("Invalid input format. Use 'a1->b2'.");
      }
    }
  }

  private Place parsePlace(String s) throws Exception {
    if (s.length() < 2) throw new Exception();
    int x = s.charAt(0) - 'a';
    int y = Integer.parseInt(s.substring(1)) - 1;
    Place place = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
    place.setX(x);
    place.setY(y);
    return place;
  }

```java
   * Summary: Ensures both the source and destination coordinates of the move are within the boundaries of the game board.
   * Algorithm: 
   *   1. Retrieve board size from game.configuration.size.
   *   2. Check if source.x, source.y, destination.x, and destination.y are all >= 0 and < size.
   *   3. Return true if all coordinates are within bounds, false otherwise.
   * Related Features: None
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Configuration, Place
   * Input: game (Game), move (Move)
```

   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean validate(final Game game, final Move move)
  {
    if (game == null || move == null || game.getConfiguration() == null) {
      return false;
    }

    int size = game.getConfiguration().getSize();
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();

    if (source == null || destination == null) {
      return false;
    }

    return (source.getX() >= 0 && source.getX() < size) &&
           (source.getY() >= 0 && source.getY() < size) &&
           (destination.getX() >= 0 && destination.getX() < size) &&
           (destination.getY() >= 0 && destination.getY() < size);

   * Summary: Ensures that the source and destination squares of the move are not the same.
   * Algorithm: Compare the (x, y) coordinates of move.source and move.destination. Return true if they are different, false otherwise.
   * Related Features: None
   * Related Classes: Move, Place
   * Input: game (Game), move (Move)
   * Output: boolean, true if source and destination are different, false if they are the same.
   * Pre-condition: move must not be null.
   * Post-condition: No state change. Returns true if the move is not a nil move.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean validate(final Game game, final Move move)
  {

        return false;
    }
    
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();
    
    if (source == null || destination == null) {
        return false;
    }
    
    return !(source.getX() == destination.getX() && source.getY() == destination.getY());
  }

```java
   * Summary: Checks if the Knight's path is blocked by an intermediate piece.
   * Algorithm: 
   *   dx = abs(move.source.x - move.destination.x)
   *   dy = abs(move.source.y - move.destination.y)
   *   if (dx == 2 && dy == 1) blockingPlace = ( (move.source.x + move.destination.x) / 2, move.source.y )
   *   else if (dx == 1 && dy == 2) blockingPlace = ( move.source.x, (move.source.y + move.destination.y) / 2 )
   *   if game.getPiece(blockingPlace) is not null, return false
```

    int srcY = move.getSource().getY();
    int destX = move.getDestination().getX();
    int destY = move.getDestination().getY();
    
    int dx = Math.abs(srcX - destX);
    int dy = Math.abs(srcY - destY);
    
    Place blockingPlace = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();

      blockingPlace.setY(srcY);

      blockingPlace.setX(srcX);
      blockingPlace.setY((srcY + destY) / 2);

      return true;
    }

```java
   * Summary: Validates Archer movement and capturing constraints.
   * Algorithm: 
   * 1. Verify move is orthogonal (same x or same y).
   * 2. Calculate the number of pieces between source and destination.
   * 3. If destination is empty: return true if piece count between source and destination is 0.
   * 4. If destination has an opponent piece: return true if piece count between source and destination is 1.
   * 5. Otherwise, return false.
   * Related Features: None
```

  public boolean validate(final Game game, final Move move)
  {
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place dest = move.getDestination();
    
    int x1 = source.getX();

    int x2 = dest.getX();
    int y2 = dest.getY();
    
    // 1. Verify move is orthogonal (same x or same y)
    if (!(x1 == x2 || y1 == y2)) {
        return false;
    }
    
    // 2. Calculate the number of pieces between source and destination
    int pieceCount = 0;
    int dx = Integer.compare(x2, x1);
    int dy = Integer.compare(y2, y1);
    
    int currX = x1 + dx;
    int currY = y1 + dy;
    
    while (currX != x2 || currY != y2) {
        if (game.getPiece(currX, currY) != null) {
            pieceCount++;
        }
        currX += dx;
        currY += dy;

    // Check destination content
    Piece destPiece = game.getPiece(dest);
    
    // 3. If destination is empty: return true if piece count between source and destination is 0.
    if (destPiece == null) {

```java
   * 2. Iterate through all possible squares (x, y) on the board.
   * 3. For each target square, construct a Move(source, destination).

   *    - Global rules: VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule.
   *    - Piece-specific rules: ArcherMoveRule.

    int boardWidth = game.getConfiguration().getWidth();
    int boardHeight = game.getConfiguration().getHeight();
    
    // Rules initialization
    VacantRule vacantRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createVacantRule();

    // Iterate through all possible squares on the board
    for (int x = 0; x < boardWidth; x++) {
      for (int y = 0; y < boardHeight; y++) {
        Place destination = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
        destination.setX(x);
        destination.setY(y);
```

```java
        // EMF 中 players 被映射为 EList，直接操作集合
        if (players == null || players.size() != 2) {
            throw new InvalidConfigurationError("there must be exactly two players");
        }
        this.getPlayers().clear();
        this.getPlayers().addAll(players);

        for (int x = 0; x < size; x++) {

        center.setY(size / 2);

        }
```

```java
        center.setX(size / 2);
        center.setY(size / 2);
        this.setCentralPlace(center);
        
        if (numMovesProtection < 0) {
            throw new InvalidConfigurationError("number of moves with capture protection cannot be negative");
        }
        this.setNumMovesProtection(numMovesProtection);
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='manual'"
   * @generated
   */
  public void addInitialPiece(final Piece piece, final Place place)
  {
    // 使用 getPlayers().get(index) 访问 EList 中的元素
    if (!piece.getPlayer().equals(this.getPlayers().get(0)) && !piece.getPlayer().equals(this.getPlayers().get(1))) {
        throw new assignment.protocol.exception.InvalidConfigurationError("the player of the piece is unknown");
    }
    
    // 使用 getX(), getY() 和 getSize() 获取属性
    if (place.getX() >= this.getSize() || place.getY() >= this.getSize() || place.getX() < 0 || place.getY() < 0) {
        throw new assignment.protocol.exception.InvalidConfigurationError("the place (" + place.getX() + ", " + place.getY() + ") must be inside the gameboard");
    }
    
    // EMF 默认的 equals 往往是引用比较，保险起见采用坐标值比对
    Place central = this.getCentralPlace();
    if (central != null && place.getX() == central.getX() && place.getY() == central.getY()) {
        throw new assignment.protocol.exception.InvalidConfigurationError("piece cannot be put at central place initially");
    }
    
    // 获取二维数组并赋值
    edu.pa20.Piece[][] board = this.getInitialBoard();
    if (board != null) {
        board[place.getX()][place.getY()] = piece;
    }
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='manual'"
   * @generated
   */
  public void addInitialPiece(final Piece piece, final int x, final int y)
  {
    // 使用 EMF Factory 实例化 Place
    Place tempPlace = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
    tempPlace.setX(x);
    tempPlace.setY(y);
    
    // 调用已经适配好的 addInitialPiece(Piece piece, Place place)
    this.addInitialPiece(piece, tempPlace);
  }
```

```java
        }
        this.setSize(size);
        
        // EMF 中 players 被映射为 EList，直接操作集合
        if (players == null || players.size() != 2) {
            throw new InvalidConfigurationError("there must be exactly two players");
        }
        this.getPlayers().clear();
        this.getPlayers().addAll(players);
        
        // 初始化二维数组，使用 EDataType 中定义的 instanceClassName (edu.pa20.Piece)
        edu.pa20.Piece[][] board = new edu.pa20.Piece[size][];
        for (int x = 0; x < size; x++) {
            board[x] = new edu.pa20.Piece[size];
            for (int y = 0; y < size; y++) {
                board[x][y] = null;
            }
        }
        this.setInitialBoard(board);
        
        // 使用 EMF Factory 实例化 Place
        Place center = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
        center.setX(size / 2);
        center.setY(size / 2);
        this.setCentralPlace(center);
        
        if (numMovesProtection < 0) {
            throw new InvalidConfigurationError("number of moves with capture protection cannot be negative");
        }
        this.setNumMovesProtection(numMovesProtection);
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='manual'"
   * @generated
   */
  public void addInitialPiece(final Piece piece, final Place place)
  {
    // 使用 getPlayers().get(index) 访问 EList 中的元素
    if (!piece.getPlayer().equals(this.getPlayers().get(0)) && !piece.getPlayer().equals(this.getPlayers().get(1))) {
        throw new assignment.protocol.exception.InvalidConfigurationError("the player of the piece is unknown");
    }
    
    // 使用 getX(), getY() 和 getSize() 获取属性
    if (place.getX() >= this.getSize() || place.getY() >= this.getSize() || place.getX() < 0 || place.getY() < 0) {
        throw new assignment.protocol.exception.InvalidConfigurationError("the place (" + place.getX() + ", " + place.getY() + ") must be inside the gameboard");
    }
    
    // EMF 默认的 equals 往往是引用比较，保险起见采用坐标值比对
    Place central = this.getCentralPlace();
    if (central != null && place.getX() == central.getX() && place.getY() == central.getY()) {
        throw new assignment.protocol.exception.InvalidConfigurationError("piece cannot be put at central place initially");
    }
    
    // 获取二维数组并赋值
    edu.pa20.Piece[][] board = this.getInitialBoard();
    if (board != null) {
        board[place.getX()][place.getY()] = piece;
    }
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='manual'"
   * @generated
   */
  public void addInitialPiece(final Piece piece, final int x, final int y)
  {
    // 使用 EMF Factory 实例化 Place
    Place tempPlace = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
    tempPlace.setX(x);
    tempPlace.setY(y);
    
    // 调用已经适配好的 addInitialPiece(Piece piece, Place place)
    this.addInitialPiece(piece, tempPlace);
  }
```

# Requirement
```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Requirement
```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Read the requirement and the class diagram.

3. If there is any error, correct the erroneous specification.
4. Follow the specification format. Output changed specifications only; OMIT unchanged specifications.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
JesonMor::movePiece
Summary: Executes a move on the board.
Algorithm: Update board array: set destination to source piece, set source to null. Increment numMoves.
Related Features: board, numMoves
Related Classes: Move, Piece
Input: move (Move)
Output: None.
Pre-condition: The move must be valid.
Post-condition: The board state is updated to reflect the move.

JesonMor::getAvailableMoves
Summary: Aggregates all legal moves for every piece belonging to a specific player.
Algorithm: Iterate through all squares on the board. If a piece at a square belongs to the player, call piece.getAvailableMoves(this, place) and add results to a list. Return the list.
Related Features: board
Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Move, Place
Input: player (Player)
Output: List of all valid Move objects for the player.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns a comprehensive list of all legal moves for the current player.

JesonMor::getWinner
Summary: Determines if a player has won according to game rules.
Algorithm: Check if game.numMoves >= protection. If so, check: 1) Did a Knight leave the central square? 2) Are all opponent pieces captured? If yes, return current player. If no moves are available, compare scores and return the winner.
Related Features: numMoves, board
Related Classes: Player, Piece, Move, Game
Input: lastPlayer (Player), lastPiece (Piece), lastMove (Move)
Output: The winning Player, or null if no winner yet.
Pre-condition: Called after a move is executed.
Post-condition: Returns the winner if conditions are met.

JesonMor::updateScore
Summary: Updates the score of the current player based on Manhattan distance.
Algorithm: Calculate Manhattan distance: |source.x - dest.x| + |source.y - dest.y|. Add this to player.score.
Related Features: score
Related Classes: Player, Piece, Move, Place
Input: player (Player), piece (Piece), move (Move)
Output: None.
Pre-condition: Move must be valid.
Post-condition: Player's score is updated.

JesonMor::start
Summary: Initializes and runs the main game loop.
Algorithm: Initialize board from Configuration. Loop: fetch player moves, prompt for next move, validate, execute move, update score, check win condition, switch turns.
Related Features: board, numMoves, currentPlayer
Related Classes: Configuration, Player, Game
Input: None.
Output: The winning Player.
Pre-condition: Configuration must be loaded.
Post-condition: The game loop terminates when a winner is decided.

# Operation Specifications
JesonMor::movePiece
Summary: Executes a move on the board.
Algorithm: Update board array: set destination to source piece, set source to null. Increment numMoves.
Related Features: board, numMoves
Related Classes: Move, Piece
Input: move (Move)
Output: None.
Pre-condition: The move must be valid.
Post-condition: The board state is updated to reflect the move.

JesonMor::getAvailableMoves
Summary: Aggregates all legal moves for every piece belonging to a specific player.
Algorithm: Iterate through all squares on the board. If a piece at a square belongs to the player, call piece.getAvailableMoves(this, place) and add results to a list. Return the list.
Related Features: board
Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Move, Place
Input: player (Player)
Output: List of all valid Move objects for the player.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns a comprehensive list of all legal moves for the current player.

JesonMor::getWinner
Summary: Determines if a player has won according to game rules.
Algorithm: Check if game.numMoves >= protection. If so, check: 1) Did a Knight leave the central square? 2) Are all opponent pieces captured? If yes, return current player. If no moves are available, compare scores and return the winner.
Related Features: numMoves, board
Related Classes: Player, Piece, Move, Game
Input: lastPlayer (Player), lastPiece (Piece), lastMove (Move)
Output: The winning Player, or null if no winner yet.
Pre-condition: Called after a move is executed.
Post-condition: Returns the winner if conditions are met.

JesonMor::updateScore
Summary: Updates the score of the current player based on Manhattan distance.
Algorithm: Calculate Manhattan distance: |source.x - dest.x| + |source.y - dest.y|. Add this to player.score.
Related Features: score
Related Classes: Player, Piece, Move, Place
Input: player (Player), piece (Piece), move (Move)
Output: None.
Pre-condition: Move must be valid.
Post-condition: Player's score is updated.

JesonMor::start
Summary: Initializes and runs the main game loop.
Algorithm: Initialize board from Configuration. Loop: fetch player moves, prompt for next move, validate, execute move, update score, check win condition, switch turns.
Related Features: board, numMoves, currentPlayer
Related Classes: Configuration, Player, Game
Input: None.
Output: The winning Player.
Pre-condition: Configuration must be loaded.
Post-condition: The game loop terminates when a winner is decided.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

FirstNMovesProtectionRule::validate
Summary: Validates that no captures occur during the protection phase.
Algorithm: If game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection, check if destination square contains an opponent's piece. If it does, return false (invalid capture). Otherwise, return true.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: Game, Move, Configuration
Input: game (Game), move (Move)
Output: boolean (true if move is not a capture during protection, false otherwise).
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Ensures capturing is prohibited when the move count is below the protection threshold.

```text
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools

  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
FirstNMovesProtectionRule::validate
Summary: Validates that no captures occur during the protection phase.
Algorithm: If game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection, check if destination square contains an opponent's piece. If it does, return false (invalid capture). Otherwise, return true.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: Game, Move, Configuration
Input: game (Game), move (Move)
Output: boolean (true if move is not a capture during protection, false otherwise).
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Ensures capturing is prohibited when the move count is below the protection threshold.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

```text
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).
```

# Operation Specifications
ArcherMoveRule::validate
Summary: Validates Archer-specific movement (orthogonal sliding and jumping capture).
Algorithm: Calculate deltaX and deltaY. If move is not orthogonal, return false. If non-capturing, ensure all squares between source and destination are empty. If capturing, ensure exactly one piece exists between source and destination.
Related Features: None
Related Classes: Game, Move, Piece
Input: game (Game), move (Move)
Output: boolean (true if valid, false otherwise).
Pre-condition: Move is within board boundaries.
Post-condition: Validates that the move follows Archer movement constraints.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

```text
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Requirement
```text
 Overview
  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.
  
  Functional Requirements
  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)
  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.
  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.
  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).
  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.
  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. Protection is active when
  game.numMoves < numMovesProtection (strictly less than); no winner can be declared during protection.
  Once game.numMoves >= numMovesProtection, protection ends and a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)
  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.
  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).
  Move Generation: Each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, source) method is responsible
  for returning the final list of legal moves for that piece. It must apply ALL
  applicable rules internally:
  - Global rules: source not vacant (VacantRule), source ≠ destination (NilMoveRule),
    within board boundaries (OutOfBoundaryRule), destination not friendly (OccupiedRule),
    and protection period check (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  - Piece-specific rules: Knight applies KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule;
    Archer applies ArcherMoveRule. A piece does NOT validate rules belonging to
    other piece types.
  Game.getAvailableMoves(player) simply iterates over all pieces belonging to the
  player, calls each piece's getAvailableMoves(game, position), and aggregates
  the results without additional filtering.
  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.
  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)
  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).
  Protection Rule: Protection is active when game.numMoves < configuration.numMovesProtection.
  During protection, no piece can be captured (FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
  The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.
  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).
  Board Display and Coordinates
  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x = column, y = row, both 0-based from
  bottom-left). Board reads should go through Game.getPiece(Place) or Game.getPiece(int x, int y). Board writes
  (e.g., in movePiece) should directly manipulate the 2D array via Game.getBoard()[x][y] = piece / null.
  There is no Game.setPiece() method. Direct indexing into board[][] is allowed for write operations in Game subclasses.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) prompts the user
  to choose a move from the list of available (already-validated legal) moves.

  Input format: The user enters a move as a coordinate "source->destination" (e.g., "a1->b2" means moving the piece at column a, row 1
  to column b, row 2).
  Coordinate parsing rules:
  - Column letter: 'a' maps to x=0, 'b' to x=1, 'c' to x=2, etc.
  - Row number: '1' maps to y=0, '2' to y=1, '3' to y=2, etc. (1-based to 0-based)
  - Parse source and destination separately using these rules.
  Validation: After parsing, the ConsolePlayer must verify that the parsed move
  (with matching source and destination coordinates) exists in availableMoves.
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```

```text
  If the input is invalid (wrong format, out of bounds, source has no piece,
  move not in availableMoves, etc.), print an error message and re-prompt
  (loop until a valid coordinate input is provided).

  External Knowledge and Tools
  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:
  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).
  InvalidConfigurationError:  Throw this when encountering invalid initialization parameters.
```
